## Why This Process Is Required

PM-16 is required because Lead Lab has a fixed program-start constraint of 2026-09-11, a conditional go/no-go target of 2026-09-04, a conditional launch target of 2026-09-07, and multiple unresolved environment, access, operations, content, and approval dependencies. The current schedule is not baselined, and the schedule and milestone artifact owner and location are not recorded. [Sources: `projects/lead-lab/CONTEXT.md`, Status and Deadline; `projects/lead-lab/pm-control/project-control.md`, lines 12-19 and 46-50; `projects/lead-lab/pm-control/artifact-index.md`, line 14; `projects/lead-lab/pm-control/runs/2026-08-21-pm-17-develop-schedule/stages/04-validate-and-review/review-record.md`, findings 1-7]

PM-17 (Develop Schedule) is an explicit downstream dependency. Its existing run produced a conditional forecast but could not calculate durations, resource calendars, owners, or float. PM-16 must define the management method and review rules before that forecast can be refreshed or considered for baseline review. [Sources: `projects/lead-lab/pm-control/runs/2026-08-21-pm-17-develop-schedule/stages/02-assemble-evidence/evidence-package.md`, lines 56-58; `projects/lead-lab/pm-control/runs/2026-08-21-pm-17-develop-schedule/stages/04-validate-and-review/review-record.md`, lines 18-22; `workspaces/alson-pm-control/references/processes/schedule.md`, PM-16 and PM-17 rows]

## Tailored Schedule Management Approach

The following controls are proposed for assessment in Stage 02 and drafting in Stage 03. They are not approved project controls or baseline changes. [Source: `workspaces/alson-pm-control/references/processes/schedule.md`, PM-16 row; `workspaces/alson-pm-control/references/authority-rules.md`, lines 23-30]

| Control area | Proposed approach |
|---|---|
| Schedule method | Use rolling-wave planning with work packages, activities, milestones, dependencies, gate entry conditions, and fallback triggers. Use detailed planning only where evidence supports it. |
| Planning horizon | Maintain detailed control through the 2026-08-25 Gate 1 reassessment and the next evidence-driven decision point. Keep the 2026-09-04 go/no-go and 2026-09-07 launch as conditional targets until their prerequisites are evidenced. [Sources: `projects/lead-lab/pm-control/registers/decision-log.md`, D-22; `projects/lead-lab/pm-control/project-control.md`, lines 17-19; `projects/lead-lab/pm-control/runs/2026-08-21-pm-17-develop-schedule/stages/04-validate-and-review/review-record.md`, lines 26-32] |
| Schedule source | Assess whether the existing delivery plan, the control-root schedule approach, or a combined carrier should hold durable schedule-management rules. Do not select an owner or canonical location in Stage 01. [Sources: `projects/lead-lab/artifacts/lead-lab-web-app-delivery-plan.md`, lines 84-97; `projects/lead-lab/pm-control/artifact-index.md`, line 14] |
| Update cadence | Propose event-driven updates after a material change, failed gate, new dependency, or forecast movement, with formal review at Gate 1 and before the 2026-09-04 go/no-go. A recurring weekly cadence is not configured in the project records. [Sources: `projects/lead-lab/pm-control/project-control.md`, lines 17-19; `projects/lead-lab/pm-control/process-register.md`, PM-17 row; `projects/lead-lab/pm-control/registers/decision-log.md`, D-22] |
| Measurement | Compare milestone and activity state against planned dates or windows, entry and exit conditions, dependency status, evidence readiness, forecast confidence, and fallback readiness. Do not use baseline variance or earned-value measures until a schedule baseline is explicitly approved. [Sources: `projects/lead-lab/pm-control/runs/2026-08-21-pm-17-develop-schedule/stages/03-perform-process/draft-output.md`, lines 14-18 and 55-69; `projects/lead-lab/pm-control/project-control.md`, line 49] |
| Dependency treatment | Each critical dependency must have a visible status, needed-by point, impact if unmet, evidence source, and decision or action path. Do not change dependency status in this run without PM direction. [Sources: `projects/lead-lab/pm-control/registers/dependencies-log.md`, lines 8-18; `workspaces/alson-pm-control/references/authority-rules.md`, lines 20-30] |
| Tolerance and escalation | Numeric schedule tolerances are not configured. Proposed trigger for PM review: any movement of a go/no-go or launch target, any failed gate, or any unresolved critical-path dependency. [Sources: `projects/lead-lab/pm-control/project-control.md`, lines 68-76; `projects/lead-lab/pm-control/runs/2026-08-21-pm-17-develop-schedule/stages/04-validate-and-review/review-record.md`, lines 26-32] |
| Baseline rule | Keep dates conditional until Gate 1, staging, participant access, production preparation, resource ownership, and final approval timing are evidenced. Do not establish a schedule baseline in this run without explicit PM approval after Stage 04. [Sources: `projects/lead-lab/pm-control/runs/2026-08-21-pm-17-develop-schedule/stages/03-perform-process/draft-output.md`, lines 67-69; `projects/lead-lab/pm-control/runs/2026-08-21-pm-17-develop-schedule/stages/05-reconcile/reconciliation-record.md`, lines 20-27; `workspaces/alson-pm-control/references/authority-rules.md`, lines 32-42] |

## Minimum Output

1. A schedule management approach covering method, schedule source, planning horizon, update cadence, measurement rules, dependency treatment, tolerance, escalation, and baseline conditions.
2. A milestone and gate control method linked to the approved scope, current conditional forecast, and fallback plan.
3. A decision-ready record of missing schedule ownership, calendars, durations, and evidence, without inventing values.
4. An artifact need assessment for the PM-16 candidates, with no canonical index change before Stage 05.

The minimum output is derived from the PM-16 recipe and the current PM-17 evidence gaps. [Sources: `workspaces/alson-pm-control/references/processes/schedule.md`, PM-16 row; `projects/lead-lab/pm-control/runs/2026-08-21-pm-17-develop-schedule/stages/04-validate-and-review/review-record.md`, lines 18-22]

## Trigger And Review Point

The immediate review trigger is the 2026-08-25 Gate 1 environment and ownership reassessment. The schedule method should then support a conditional forecast refresh before the 2026-09-04 go/no-go review. [Sources: `projects/lead-lab/pm-control/registers/decision-log.md`, D-22; `projects/lead-lab/pm-control/project-control.md`, lines 17-19; `projects/lead-lab/pm-control/process-register.md`, PM-17 row]

Stage 04 must validate whether the proposed method is supported by visible scope, dependencies, calendars, ownership evidence, governance rules, and current source records. The run must stop after Stage 04 for explicit PM direction before any canonical process metadata, artifact index entry, schedule-management record, owner, threshold, or baseline state is changed. [Source: `workspaces/alson-pm-control/references/process-execution-rules.md`, lines 14-29]

## Authority Boundary

The agent may prepare the schedule-management approach and proposed artifact treatment through Stage 04. The PM must direct any owner assignment, committed date, tolerance approval, dependency-state change, schedule baseline, external delivery-plan change, scope change, or canonical reconciliation. LeadLab Director remains the final launch acceptance authority.
